title: List Item
description: Application row content, actions, context menus, icon overrides, disabled behaviour, accessibility, and native platform expression.

blocks.text: List Item presents one tappable application row with a primary headline, optional supporting text, an optional leading identity, and an optional trailing affordance. It renders as a genuine SwiftUI button row on iOS and a Material 3 List Item on Android.

<firstlight:list-item
    headline="Account"
    supporting="Manage your profile and security"
    leading-icon="person"
    leading-icon-ios="person.crop.circle"
    leading-icon-android="account_circle"
    trailing-icon="chevron-right"
    trailing-icon-ios="chevron.right"
    trailing-icon-android="chevron_right"
    a11y-hint="Opens account settings"
    :disabled="! $canManageAccount"
    @press="openAccount"
/>
List Item is self-closing. Its content is semantic rather than a general child slot: arbitrary text, controls, and layouts cannot be nested inside the row.

blocks.text: Choose at most one leading source: icon, avatar, monogram, or label. Choose at most one trailing affordance: icon, text, or status. Supporting text and both edges may be omitted for a headline-only row.

runs.text: Blade examples use kebab-case names. The equivalent
aliases are also accepted for parity with NativePHP authoring.
The new attributes also accept matching camelCase aliases and fluent setters:

blocks.text:
<firstlight:list-item
    headline="Alex Morgan"
    supporting="Discharge"
    leading-label="4B-12"
    trailing-status="Waiting to sync"
    trailing-status-tone="warning"
    state="pending-removal"
    state-label="Discharge waiting to sync"
    @press="openPatient(42)"
/>

The leading label and trailing status join the default spoken row name. An explicit

is still announced as state. The status is not a nested action or separate accessibility stop. At accessibility text sizes it moves below the headline/supporting text so the headline remains readable.

blocks.text: Use Mobile UI text/columns for read-only key-value content, not a List Item with a fake press handler. For a comparison, PHP decides match, mismatch or unknown; Status Label communicates the result with words as well as a mark:

<native:column class="w-full gap-2">
    <native:text class="text-theme-on-surface">Patient: {{ $patientName }}</native:text>
    <native:text class="text-theme-on-surface">Date of birth: {{ $formattedDob }}</native:text>
    <native:text class="text-theme-on-surface">Label identifier: {{ $labelIdentifier }}</native:text>
    <native:text class="text-theme-on-surface">On file: {{ $fileIdentifier }}</native:text>
    @if ($comparison === 'match')
        <firstlight:status-label label="Matches" tone="success" icon="check" icon-ios="checkmark" />
    @elseif ($comparison === 'mismatch')
        <firstlight:status-label label="Does not match" tone="warning" />
    @else
        <firstlight:status-label label="Not compared" tone="neutral" />
    @endif
</native:column>
The app supplies the display values and comparison result. This is ordinary native composition, not a new catalogue layout or validation engine.

<firstlight:list>
    <firstlight:list-item

            ['method' => 'requestDestroy(42)', 'label' => 'Delete', 'role' => 'destructive'],
            ['method' => 'flag(42)', 'label' => 'Flag'],

    />
</firstlight:list>

blocks.text: Publishing a different menu, or disabling the row, replaces what the next menu shows without emitting an event. Android closes an open menu when that happens. An open iOS system menu can stay on screen until dismissed, but its items then emit nothing.
Context menus and swipe actions can be combined. Submenus, section titles, checkmark or selected state, keyboard shortcuts, custom previews, and per-item colours are not supported.

blocks.text: Icon resolution happens in PHP. The shared icon is the deterministic fallback; the iOS or Android override wins on its platform. A typed Android symbol keeps its filled or outlined variant in the native wire metadata. Overrides without their shared fallback are invalid.

blocks.text: Independent trailing buttons, switches, checkboxes, radio buttons, overflow menus, and other embedded targets are excluded. Swipe actions and the long-press context menu are separate from these decorative trailing affordances.

runs.text: By default, assistive technology combines the headline and supporting text as the row's accessible name.
adds context. The complete row is one button node with disabled state and a minimum interaction target of 44 points on iOS or 48 dp on Android.

blocks.text: Leading avatars, monograms, icons, and trailing content are decorative and do not add duplicate VoiceOver or TalkBack stops. Dynamic Type, Android font scaling, right-to-left layout, native contrast, focus, and press feedback remain platform-owned.

Inside List, swipe actions are available through native VoiceOver actions and TalkBack custom actions without performing a swipe gesture. Revealed Android buttons also expose their visible labels and button roles.

Every enabled context menu item is also a VoiceOver action and a TalkBack custom action named by its label, so screen-reader users can run it from the Actions rotor or TalkBack actions menu without a long press. Disabled items are not offered as actions. TalkBack's own long-press action still opens the visible menu. Menu items follow the reading direction, including RTL, and their text scales with Dynamic Type and Android font scaling.

runs.text: Firstlight rejects missing or blank headlines, missing

, blank accessible labels/hints, non-boolean disabled values, invalid icon override types, icon overrides without shared fallbacks, ambiguous leading or trailing content, and content slots. It also rejects overline text, embedded controls, independent trailing actions, malformed or unlabelled swipe or context menu descriptors, raw
, navigation directives, model or selection state, loading and validation props, non-icon colours, elevation, typography, and per-platform layout escape hatches.

does not conflict with a trailing icon. Other non-string values remain invalid. Overline is not part of Firstlight's row contract.
